top.line: The php2shell story at 8pm, and a guided tour of the site built in a day to track it.
top.para: At 8pm UK time the fix is out, sixteen agencies say install it, attackers are trying, and no break-in is confirmed. The Dutch inventory lists 724 products, 61 fixed. Behind it is php.oct.2026.newsroom.sgit.ai: 34 versions in one day, 13 agents, an evidence vault anyone can read, graded claims and versions of everything.

in-short.line: Seven lines: the fix, attempts, no confirmed break-in, the inventory, a site in a day, a public vault, versions.
in-short.para: Install PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Attempts number in the millions, one seen four days early. No break-in confirmed and not on the US exploited list. 724 products listed, 61 fixed. The site was built today in 34 versions, rests on a public vault, and records versions so updates can be compared.

stands.line: Fix since 21 October, unanimous advice to install, mass attempts, no confirmed compromise, 724 inventory rows.
stands.para: Two flaws rated 9.2, fixed in four releases on 21 October; 8.1 and older have no fix. Disclosure was 21 October, not 22, which our section had wrong. Agencies agree on patching but differ on going offline. Cloudflare reports millions of attempts and Amazon one on 17 October. No compromise is confirmed and the US catalogue does not list the flaws.

unknown.line: Unknown: break-ins, whether the fix is complete, unpatched counts, the leak, and the 70% figure.
unknown.para: Nobody yet knows whether any site was broken into before patching, or whether the fix is complete; that report is graded not shown. The number of unpatched systems is an open contradiction. The source of the 20 October leak is unknown, and 70% is roughly PHP's share of websites, not a measure of risk.

day.line: From v0.1.0 at 09:27 to v0.5.5 at 19:04 UTC: 34 versions, 62 commits, 17 team members.
day.para: The site went from its first to its thirty-fourth version in one day, with two version lines merged. Its team page lists two people and 13 agents, each with a role, rules and shipped work, and a board of 89 tasks, 25 done. The editor directed by memo; the agents captured, built, checked and released.

tour.line: Eleven stops: readers, phone, evidence, graded claims, graph, code, patching, stories, versions, vaults, readers.
tour.para: A plain-English front page and fifteen briefings; Now and Ask on a phone with your own key; a public vault of 184 sources and a source watch of 328 pages; 70 claims graded, two refuted, ten contradictions; a 209-node graph; the fix read in php-src; the inventory hour by hour; stories; 110 versioned sections; eight vaults; synthetic readers.

map.line: A snapshot of every version, head, count and file hash at 8pm, so the next update is a diff.
map.para: Published with this article: the site's version and commit, the vault, source watch and inventory heads and counts, the fact-check run, the outside checks, every count in the tour and the hash of all 46 data files. The next update takes the same snapshot, and the difference is the update.

lessons.line: The machinery outran the evidence, grading caught our own error, and versions make updates exact.
lessons.para: The vault's last capture is 11:34 UTC while the site released every twelve minutes, so its account is a morning account and scheduled capture comes next; uncaptured reports are not facts. The fact-check desk refuted a date in our own section, now corrected. Versioned sections and files turn what changed into an exact answer.

limits.line: Facts are as captured, mostly morning; two checks are mine at 19:00; counts at v0.5.5; grades are one run.
limits.para: The story facts come from captures ending at 11:34 UTC. The exploited-vulnerability catalogue and php.net were read directly at 19:00 and are not captured. Counts are from the site's data at 19:04 UTC. The grades are one desk's single run, and synthetic readers are a test instrument, not readers.

sources.line: The site and its repository, the public vault, the Dutch inventory, CISA and php.net, and screenshots.
